source: Diffusion and Osmosis Diagnostic Test (DODT), Odom & Barrow 1995, J. Research in Science Teaching 32:45-61; full items in Odom 1995, American Biology Teacher 57(7):409-415, Appendix A | 12 two-tier items (content tier + reason tier); each pair appears as consecutive items (orig_label Na = content, Nb = reason). No answer key published in source; correct_label left null. Transcribed from local md 2026-07-03. Some items reference figures described inline.

items.text: Suppose there is a large beaker full of clear water and a drop of blue dye is added to the beaker of water. Eventually the water will turn a light blue color. The process responsible for blue dye becoming evenly distributed throughout the water is:

options.label: A
options.text: Osmosis

options.label: B
options.text: Diffusion

options.label: C
options.text: A reaction between water and dye

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: The lack of a membrane means that osmosis and diffusion cannot occur.

options.label: B
options.text: There is movement of particles between regions of different concentrations.

options.label: C
options.text: The dye separates into small particles and mixes with water.

options.label: D
options.text: The water moves from one region to another.

items.text: During the process of diffusion, particles will generally move from:

options.label: A
options.text: High to low concentrations

options.label: B
options.text: Low to high concentrations

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: There are too many particles crowded into one area, therefore they move to an area with more room.

options.label: B
options.text: Particles in areas of greater concentration are more likely to bounce toward other areas.

options.label: C
options.text: The particles tend to move until the two areas are isotonic and then the particles stop moving.

options.label: D
options.text: There is a greater chance of the particles repelling each other.

items.text: As the difference in concentration between two areas increases, the rate of diffusion:

options.label: A
options.text: Decreases

options.label: B
options.text: Increases

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: There is less room for the particles to move.

options.label: B
options.text: If the concentration is high enough, the particles will spread less and the rate will be slowed.

options.label: C
options.text: The molecules want to spread out.

options.label: D
options.text: The greater likelihood of random motion into other regions.

items.text: A glucose solution can be made more concentrated by:

options.label: A
options.text: Adding more water

options.label: B
options.text: Adding more glucose

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: The more water there is, the more glucose it will take to saturate the solution.

options.label: B
options.text: Concentration means the dissolving of something.

options.label: C
options.text: It increases the number of dissolved particles.

options.label: D
options.text: For a solution to be more concentrated, one must add more liquid.

items.text: If a small amount of sugar is added to a container of water and allowed to set for a very long period of time without stirring, the sugar molecules will:

options.label: A
options.text: Be more concentrated on the bottom of the container

options.label: B
options.text: Be evenly distributed throughout the container

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: There is movement of particles from a high to low concentration.

options.label: B
options.text: The sugar is heavier than water and will sink.

options.label: C
options.text: Sugar dissolves poorly or not at all in water.

options.label: D
options.text: There will be more time for settling.

items.text: Suppose you add a drop of blue dye to a container of clear water and after several hours the entire container turns light blue. At this time, the molecules of dye:

options.label: A
options.text: Have stopped moving

options.label: B
options.text: Continue to move around randomly

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: The entire container is the same color; if the dye molecules were still moving, the container would be different shades of blue.

options.label: B
options.text: If the dye molecules stopped, they would settle to the bottom of the container.

options.label: C
options.text: Molecules are always moving.

options.label: D
options.text: This is a liquid; if it were solid the molecules would stop moving.

items.text: Suppose there are two large beakers with equal amounts of clear water at two different temperatures (Beaker 1 at 25°C, Beaker 2 at 35°C). A drop of green dye is added to each. Which beaker became light green first?

options.label: A
options.text: Beaker 1

options.label: B
options.text: Beaker 2

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: The lower temperature breaks down the dye.

options.label: B
options.text: The dye molecules move faster at higher temperatures.

options.label: C
options.text: The cold temperature speeds up the molecules.

options.label: D
options.text: It helps the molecules to expand.

items.text: Two columns of water are separated by a membrane through which only water can pass. Side 1 contains dye and water; Side 2 contains pure water. After two hours, the water level in Side 1 will be:

options.label: A
options.text: Higher

options.label: B
options.text: Lower

options.label: C
options.text: The same height

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: Water will move from the hypertonic to hypotonic solution.

options.label: B
options.text: The concentration of water molecules is less on Side 1.

options.label: C
options.text: Water will become isotonic.

options.label: D
options.text: Water moves from low to high concentration.

items.text: Side 1 (10% salt solution) is ___ to Side 2 (15% salt solution).

options.label: A
options.text: Hypotonic

options.label: B
options.text: Hypertonic

options.label: C
options.text: Isotonic

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: Water is hypertonic to most things.

options.label: B
options.text: Isotonic means "the same."

options.label: C
options.text: Water moves from a high to a low.

options.label: D
options.text: There are fewer dissolved particles on Side 1.

items.text: A plant cell that lives in fresh water is placed in a beaker of 25% salt water solution. The central vacuole would:

options.label: A
options.text: Increase in size

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease in size

options.label: C
options.text: Remain the same size

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: Salt absorbs the water from the central vacuole.

options.label: B
options.text: Water will move from the vacuole to the salt water solution.

options.label: C
options.text: The salt will enter the vacuole.

options.label: D
options.text: Salt solution outside the cell cannot affect the vacuole inside the cell.

items.text: Suppose you killed the plant cell with poison and placed the dead cell in a 25% salt water solution. Osmosis and diffusion would:

options.label: A
options.text: Not occur

options.label: B
options.text: Continue

options.label: C
options.text: Only diffusion would continue

options.label: D
options.text: Only osmosis would continue

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: The cell would stop functioning.

options.label: B
options.text: The cell does not have to be alive.

options.label: C
options.text: Osmosis is not random, while diffusion is a random process.

options.label: D
options.text: Osmosis and diffusion require cell energy.

items.text: All cell membranes are:

options.label: A
options.text: Semipermeable

options.label: B
options.text: Permeable

items.text: The reason for my answer is:

options.label: A
options.text: They allow some substances to pass.

options.label: B
options.text: They allow some substances to enter, but they prevent any substance from leaving.

options.label: C
options.text: The membrane requires nutrients to live.

options.label: D
options.text: They allow ALL nutrients to pass.
